title: Tenant Attestation & SIEM Enrichment Spec — RBAC v2, Audit Schema, Evidence Automation
content:
Purpose:
This working spec defines a tenant attestation model and a SIEM enrichment pipeline that complements RBAC v2. It is meant to:
- Provide a minimal, auditable evidence set for role assignments and policy changes across hosting tiers (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Define an export/mapping layer (audit schema -> SIEM) that preserves context for downstream detection and compliance automation.
- Describe an evidence automation flow (snapshots, attestation records, proof-of-state) that can be consumed by Security, Compliance, and Customer Audit teams.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to all account/tenant management activities and service account bindings touching inference control planes, keys, billing, network egress controls, and model onboarding flows.
- Targets three deployment scopes: Hosted (multi-tenant managed control plane), Dedicated (customer-reserved infra w/ Redwood-managed control plane), Private (VPC/on-prem with customer control plane).
- Not a replacement for full SIEM schema design; focuses on enrichment fields and evidence surfacing needed for RBAC attestation and tenant-level investigations.

High-level principles:
- Least privilege by default; ephemeral elevation through short-lived grants and approval-backed attestation records.
- Treat role bindings as first-class auditable artifacts: every change gets an attestation id and snapshot.
- Keep evidence narrow and reproducible: source references (user/service-account id, binding id, commit/tag, policy version), human justification, and cryptographic proof (hash of snapshot file).
- Preserve tenant isolation: exports for Hosted must mask cross-tenant sensitive content and include tenant-id context; Dedicated/Private exports can contain fuller context subject to customer contractual requirements.

Roles matrix (canonical short names):
- PLATFORM_ADMIN: platform-wide control; manage infra, billing, org-level config.
- TENANT_ADMIN: tenant-level user and policy management, model uploads within tenant.
- TENANT_VIEWER: read-only visibility into tenant resources.
- SRE_ONCALL: incident actions (restarts, scaling, route changes) scoped by environment.
- SUPPORT_AGENT: triage tenant issues via controlled escalation path; no secret/key access.
- MODEL_ONBOARDER: permission to register/validate new models for serving; subject to QA gating.
- AUDIT_READER: access to evidence snapshots and attestation logs.
- KMS_OPERATOR: rotate/wrap keys for customer-controlled KMS (private/dedicated only).
- BILLING_ADMIN: view/modify billing configs and invoices.

Environment-by-environment mapping (high level):
- Hosted:
  - PLATFORM_ADMIN: limited to platform-level without tenant data access unless explicitly bound.
  - TENANT_ADMIN: can be Redwood-managed tenant admins (for managed customers) or customer-managed when configured.
  - SUPPORT_AGENT: granted time-limited ramp access via approved attestation; all sessions recorded.
  - KMS_OPERATOR: never granted to Redwood operators for customer keys; use envelope-wrapping proxies.
- Dedicated:
  - Many platform roles are scoped to the dedicated pool. PLATFORM_ADMIN can operate infrastructure but tenant data access remains segregated.
  - KMS_OPERATOR may require cross-team attestation if Redwood manages keys per contract.
- Private:
  - Most operational roles are customer-managed. Redwood support actions must be explicitly authorized and accompanied by attestation artifacts and contract-scoped escalation.

Role binding attributes (what we record for each binding):
- binding_id (unique UUID)
- tenant_id (or org id)
- principal_type (user, service_account, group)
- principal_id (email or service id)
- role (canonical short name)
- scope (global, tenant, resource path)
- grant_method (manual, api, sync-from-identity-provider)
- created_by (actor id)
- created_at (ISO8601)
- expires_at (ISO8601 or null)
- justification (free text, can be structured form id)
- attestation_id (link to evidence snapshot)
- policy_version (semver or hash)
- previous_binding_snapshot (hash)

Audit event schema (core fields to emit from control plane audit stream):
- event_id: string
- timestamp: ISO8601
- tenant_id: string
- actor: {type: string, id: string}  --> store as flattened 'actor_type' and 'actor_id' in exports
- action: string (e.g., role.bind, role.unbind, key.rotate, model.upload, model.deploy)
- target: {type: string, id: string} -> flattened as 'target_type','target_id'
- binding_id: string (if applicable)
- policy_hash: string
- request_context: string (short tokenized context; not PII)
- outcome: string (success | failure | partial)
- client_ip: string (ipv4/ipv6)
- source_system: string (console | api | idp-sync | support-tool)
- correlation_id: string
- attestation_id: string (if attached)
- evidence_snapshot_hash: string
- cloud_region: string
- additional_tags: comma-separated list
Notes: the export flattens nested actor/target objects into simple key:value pairs to align with SIEM ingestion best practices. PII fields must be redacted per data classification rules before leaving hosted tenancy boundaries.

SIEM export mapping (recommended column/field names):
- ecs.event.id -> event_id
- @timestamp -> timestamp
- redwood.tenant.id -> tenant_id
- redwood.actor.type -> actor_type
- redwood.actor.id -> actor_id
- redwood.action -> action
- redwood.target.type -> target_type
- redwood.target.id -> target_id
- redwood.binding.id -> binding_id
- redwood.policy.hash -> policy_hash
- redwood.attestation.id -> attestation_id
- redwood.evidence.hash -> evidence_snapshot_hash
- network.client.ip -> client_ip
- cloud.region -> cloud_region
- service.name -> source_system
- event.outcome -> outcome
- redwood.tags -> additional_tags

Notes on masking and tenancy:
- Hosted: redact principal emails for users outside of compliance-approved scans; replace with principal_id hashed with tenant-specific salt (preserve deterministic mapping for investigation within tenant).
- Dedicated/Private: if contract allows, export full principal identity. Otherwise follow hosted masking rules.

Evidence automation flow (attestation lifecycle):
1) Binding change detected (API, console, IDP sync) -> create provisional audit event and provisional binding snapshot.
2) If change meets policy thresholds (privileged role, cross-tenant, KMS access), create Attestation record requiring approval. Attestation record includes: binding_id, actor_id, justification form id, requester_ip, pre-change snapshot, post-change snapshot, and a snapshot_hash.
3) Approval (UI or API) attaches approver id and approval timestamp, emits attestation.approved event.
4) Evidence packaging job runs (scheduled or triggered) producing a signed, compressed evidence bundle: bundle metadata file (json), snapshot csv, policy text, and a SHA256 manifest. The job writes to the evidence store (S3/GCS path) and records evidence_store_path + bundle_hash in attestation record.
5) SIEM enrichment service picks up the attestation event and emits the flattened event with redwood.attestation.id and redwood.evidence.hash.
6) Retention and legal holds are applied at the bundle level. Retention policy: default 2 years for privileged attestation bundles; configurable per contract.

Evidence bundle minimal contents (file list):
- manifest.json (bundle_id, created_by, created_at, tenant_id, bundle_hash)
- binding_snapshot.csv (flattened binding attributes)
- audit_events.csv (raw control-plane events that led to attestation)
- policy_text.md (policy version and text)
- approval_log.txt (approver ids and timestamps)
- signed.manifest.sig (signature of manifest.json by platform key)

Proof model: hash(manifest.json) is recorded in attestation record. Platform signs manifest with a rotating platform key and stores signature with bundle. Customers may request proof-of-integrity during audits.

Sample policy templates (text snippets; adapt to environment and IAM system):
- Tenant-level read-only (hosted):
  "Allow:TenantViewer -> resources:tenant/* -> actions:[read, list]"

- Support time-limited escalation (grant via attestation):
  "Allow:SupportAgent -> resources:tenant/{tenant_id}/support-sessions/* -> actions:[open_session] -> constraints:[time_window=2h, approval=attestation:{attestation_id}]"

- Model onboarder with QA gating:
  "Allow:ModelOnboarder -> resources:models/* -> actions:[upload, submit_for_validation] -> constraints:[requires_tag:qa-reviewed=false]"

- KMS wrap-only (dedicated/private):
  "Allow:KMSOperator -> resources:kms/keys/{key_id} -> actions:[encrypt,wrap,key-status] -> constraints:[no-unwrap]"

Operational playbook (quick steps):
- New privileged role binding created in Hosted -> auto-generate attestation requirement -> send notification to approvers group -> if emergency flag set, attach emergency justification and require retrospective attestation within 24h.
- Support requests that require temporary tenant access: use the ephemeral session flow; create attestation before session start and emit session_id into evidence bundle.
- Cross-tenant admin tasks: disallowed unless explicit platform-level attestation is present (platform audit team verifies quarterly).

SIEM use-cases enabled by enrichment:
- Detect suspicious after-hours role escalations for tenant admins (event.action == role.bind and actor_type == user and timestamp outside business hours).
- Correlate model deploys and key rotations to identify possible exfil attempts (sequence: model.deploy -> key.rotate -> model.upload from new principal).
- Surface unapproved external support accesses (attestation absent or marked emergency with no retrospective approval).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (pilot, 4 weeks): implement binding snapshot + bundle writer in a single dev tenant; prototype SIEM mapping on staging Splunk/Elasticsearch.
- Phase 1 (hosted opt-in, 6 weeks): enable attestation requirement for top-5 privileged roles in hosted dev and staging tenants; provide tenants an opt-in toggle.
- Phase 2 (platform-wide hosted, 8 weeks): gated rollout enabling attestation enforcement and SIEM export for security team.
- Phase 3 (dedicated/private, ongoing): publish templates and helper scripts for customers; offer managed evidence packaging as paid add-on.

Open decisions / risks:
- Signature Key Management: platform signing key rotation cadence and trust model for customer audits (HSM-backed vs platform-managed).
- Masking semantics for hosted tenants: threshold for when identifying information can be included in SIEM exports for investigations.
- Retention alignment with legal: default 2 years may conflict with some customer contracts requiring longer retention.

Implementation notes and links:
- Suggested infra pieces: evidence-bundler service, attestation-service, siem-enricher lambda, evidence-store (S3/GCS with bucket per-tenant or per-region), key-signing-service (KMS/HSM).
- Example artifacts: CONFLUENCE-SEC-RBAC-V2-ATT (design page), JIRA-SEC-478 (implementation ticket), github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/rbac-v2 (reference code).

Appendix (short examples):
- Example flattened audit event line (CSV row):
  event_id,timestamp,tenant_id,actor_type,actor_id,action,target_type,target_id,binding_id,policy_hash,attestation_id,evidence_hash,outcome,client_ip,source_system,cloud_region
  e-1234,2025-11-07T14:22:01Z,tenant-47,user,alice%40example.com,role.bind,tenant,tenant-47,b-9f8a,hash:abcd1234,att-55,hash:bundle987,success,52.34.12.8,console,us-west1

- Example attestation manifest excerpt (manifest.json fields shown in plain text):
  bundle_id: bundle-20251107-0001
  tenant_id: tenant-47
  created_at: 2025-11-07T14:23:00Z
  created_by: r.patel%40redwood.company
  bundle_hash: sha256:...

Feedback requested:
- Are the proposed flattened fields sufficient for SIEM correlation work? Any missing context your detection rules require?
- Proposed masking approach for hosted tenants: is deterministic hashing per-tenant enough for your investigation workflows?
- Preferred retention defaults and legal hold APIs we should expose for customers?

Next actions:
- Security eng to spin up pilot evidence-bundler; SRE to wire SIEM staging index; Compliance to validate bundle contents.
- Schedule a walkthrough with detection engineering and support (owner: Ravi Patel).
